# DokuReader

## Last-checked: 2026-08-26


## Canonical Links

- Repository: https://github.com/doc-bricks/DokuReader
- Issues: https://github.com/doc-bricks/DokuReader/issues
- License: AGPL-3.0

## Summary

DokuReader is a local-first Tkinter desktop app for organizing document references by topic, previewing common file formats, tracking read/unread status, and exporting combined PDFs or a metadata-only JSON library.

## Audience

- Users who keep private document libraries on a local Windows desktop.
- Researchers and knowledge workers who sort PDF and Office documents by topic.
- Maintainers preparing a simple AGPL desktop app for Windows Store distribution.
- LLM agents that need the project boundary, entrypoints, and export format without reading private user data.

## Search Phrases

```text
local-first document library
topic based PDF organizer
document read status tracker
metadata-only document export
Tkinter document manager
offline PDF bundling desktop app
local document preview app
dokureader document library GitHub
local PDF reading queue
read unread document tracker
desktop document library JSON export
```

## Disambiguation

DokuReader is not a cloud document manager, hosted OCR platform, general note-taking app, or full citation-management suite. It stores references and read status for local files; LitZentrum covers the broader literature-management workflow in the same doc-bricks family.

## External Discovery Notes

- GitHub and GitHub Topic pages currently index `doc-bricks/DokuReader` directly for document-library and pdf-tools contexts.
- Broader web searches still collide with generic document, OCR, and Bricks Builder documentation results, so keep the canonical phrase `doc-bricks/DokuReader` and local-first document-library wording visible in README surfaces.
- The repo has no external directory listing beyond GitHub surfaces; editorial posts or curated Python/Tkinter desktop-app lists remain manual follow-up work.

## Local Data Boundary

- Original documents remain in their existing filesystem locations.
- App state is stored locally in `~/.dokubibliothek_state.json`.
- The `dokureader-library-v1.json` export contains topics, paths, file metadata, and read status.
- The standard JSON export does not embed document contents, PDFs, images, previews, accounts, tokens, or cloud credentials.

## Interfaces

- Desktop entrypoint: `python DokuReader.py`
- Windows launcher: `START.bat`
- Windows build launcher: `build_exe.bat`
- Export schema docs: `EXPORTFORMAT.md`
- Store docs: `STORE_LISTING.md`, `PRIVACY_POLICY.md`, `SUPPORT.md`, `store_package.json`
- Version/release readback: `RELEASE_STATUS.md`, `PORTIERUNGSPLAN.md`
- Store readiness gate: `python _WARTUNG/check_store_readiness.py --allow-blockers`
- WACK runner and parser: `python _WARTUNG/run_windows_wack.py --dry-run`

## Test And Validation

- Python tests live under `tests/` (including `test_metadata.py`, `test_release_contract.py`, `test_accessibility_contract.py`, `test_bug_regressions.py`, `test_export_format.py`, `test_store_readiness.py`, `test_windows_wack.py`, `test_store_media.py`, `test_ui_accessibility.py`; 46 collected, 46 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0).
- Web Companion tests live under `web_companion/tests/` (32 Node.js tests verified: 100% green).
- Suites are counted separately, never summed: Python 46 collected / 0 failed
  (exit 0); Web Companion 32 passed / 0 failed (exit 0); `ruff check .` clean
  (exit 0); `python tests/source_platform_smoke.py` OK (exit 0). Measured
  2026-08-26 with Python 3.12.10 on Windows.
- The former sporadic Tk initialization skip is bounded by at most three setup
  attempts. Ten independent focused runs produced 60/60 UI test passes without
  a skip. A real Tk visual smoke captured and reviewed empty, drag-and-drop and
  text-preview states; receipt: `UI_POLISH_SMOKE.json`.
- MSIX, WACK, signing and Store gates are external and remain unproven by any of
  these runs.
- Current focused validation: `python -m pytest -q` and `npm test` in `web_companion`.
- Store readiness validation: `python _WARTUNG/check_store_readiness.py --allow-blockers`
- Syntax smoke: `python -m py_compile DokuReader.py manage_translations.py translator.py _WARTUNG/generate_store_media.py _WARTUNG/check_store_readiness.py _WARTUNG/run_windows_wack.py tests/source_platform_smoke.py`
- Workflow YAML should parse before push.

## Version And Release Boundary

- Runtime development version: `DokuReader.py` `APP_VERSION=1.0.1-dev`.
- Python package metadata: `pyproject.toml` `1.0.1.dev0`.
- Windows Store package metadata: `store_package.json` `1.0.1.0`.
- No public release, signed MSIX, WACK certification, or Store submission is verified.
- The metadata-first accessibility contract covers semantic names, roles, states,
  descriptions, focus order, and read-only preview text. A controlled Tk visual
  smoke covers empty, drag-and-drop and preview layout states; it does not claim
  screen-reader, keyboard-hardware, or device acceptance.

## Safety Notes

- Do not commit local document libraries, generated releases, converted PDFs, credentials, or `~/.dokubibliothek_state.json`.
- `releases/`, build outputs, local state, SQLite files, tokens, and private/archive folders are ignored.
- Optional PyMuPDF support keeps the project in AGPL-3.0 territory unless a commercial Artifex license is used.
